items.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Do you remember the tunes that you were playing, any of the tunes?

Yeah, the pop tunes of the day, things like Don’t Blame Me. I remember that because it was the first thing I ever heard Teddy Wilson play as a solo and I loved the way he played that. I had heard him play other things. But we were playing things like China Boy, Nagasaki. Matter of fact, the tune Nagasaki had the same changes as I Got Rhythm except for the bridge, and that was where I learned rhythm changes, not from I Got Rhythm. I learned how to play the first eight bars of I Got Rhythm from Nagasaki. It was an…

all purpose bridges. But I can’t remember what the… there was… Lizer was a tune that we played. We played some Gershwin tunes. We played a lot of Ellington tunes because everybody… Ellington was from Washington. Everybody knew Ellington and loved him. There was a young player when I was in junior high school, his name was Billy White. He was a alto saxophone player and clarinetist, and when I got serious about playing music he was the guy that helped me really focus on songs like In A Sentimental Mood and he…
